note: Results published after N. J. A. Sloane's table (last modified 20 Jan 1997) that change a cell, found in the literature check of 15 Nov 2026. 'optimal': the table's value is proven optimal, so the cell is solved and left out. 'packings': line packings (n = 1) of M. Fickus, J. Jasper and D. G. Mixon, Packings in real projective spaces, SIAM J. Appl. Algebra Geom. 2 (2018) 377-409 (arXiv:1707.01858), Table 1: each gives a packing of N lines in R^m whose coherence mu is the root of the stated polynomial (coefficients from the highest degree) next to the stated rounding up of mu; its squared chordal distance is 1 - mu^2. Where it is larger than the table's value for N or fewer lines, it is the best known value (any subset of a packing is a packing). Also read: I. S. Dhillon, R. W. Heath, T. Strohmer and J. A. Tropp, Constructing packings in Grassmannian manifolds via alternating projection, Experimental Math. 17 (2008) (arXiv:0709.0535), whose real packings do not beat the table (its Table 3); D. G. Mixon and H. Parshall, Exact line packings from numerical solutions (arXiv:1902.00552), which gives exact forms of the table's packings.
